title: xorxorxor HTB
description: xorxorxor (htb, crypto) is a lattice-cipher challenge that hides a linear algebra shortcut behind a lattice/cvp disguise. each flag character is packed into a vector with random padding, multiplied by a fixed public 3x3 matrix, and offset by a "random" error vector — except that vector is generated once and reused across all 46 characters. inverting the matrix and brute-forcing the tiny 11³ error keyspace, validated against every ciphertext line at once, collapses the whole problem instantly. a clean example of how reused randomness quietly breaks otherwise sound-looking crypto, without needing any real lattice reduction.
author: z1rov

title: Helix HTB
description: Helix (HTB, Linux) is built around an industrial-automation theme with a three-stage chain. Foothold comes from CVE-2023-34468, an unauth H2 JDBC injection in Apache NiFi 1.21.0 sitting on a hidden vhost — gets you code exec as nifi. From there a leaked SSH key inside a NiFi support bundle hands you operator. A cracked PDF on that user's desktop reveals an OPC UA endpoint and the reactor's documented hazard threshold; writing straight to the writable telemetry nodes forces a fake hazard state, which tricks a sudo-gated "break-glass" console into dropping a root shell. Solid box for practicing RE-adjacent web app abuse plus a genuinely different privesc angle instead of the usual SUID/cron stuff.
author: z1rov
